title: Mars Climate Orbiter loss: metric/English-unit interface failure in ground navigation modeling
summary: NASA's MCO Mishap Investigation Board attributed the spacecraft loss to a units failure in a ground software file used by trajectory models: impulse data required as Newton-seconds was reported as pound-force-seconds, causing navigation processing to underestimate thruster effects by a factor of 4.45. The record is promoted only as an official-report-backed incident shell; it is not yet a full historical synthesis.

type_payload.system: Earth/spacecraft navigation loop involving spacecraft telemetry, ground software, interface specifications, and trajectory modeling

sequence_of_events.event: During cruise, AMD events generated data used by ground navigation software to model small forces from thruster firings.
Ground SM_FORCES output placed impulse data into AMD files using English-force units despite interface requirements for metric units.
Trajectory models processed the file as if it were metric, underestimating thruster effects over the mission cruise.
The spacecraft approached Mars substantially lower than planned and was lost after occultation during Mars Orbit Insertion.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Incorrect units in ground-software output consumed by trajectory modeling.
type_payload.root_cause_source_language: failure to use metric units in coding a ground software file used in trajectory models
contributing_factors: AMD file-format and content problems early in cruise delayed reliable use and anomaly detection.
Limited observability of the thrust effect helped mask the systematic error.
Operations navigation personnel did not have enough intimate familiarity with spacecraft attitude-control details and had not participated in earlier testing.
A contingency TCM-5 maneuver was discussed but not executed; readiness and decision criteria were not adequate.
latent_conditions: Interface-control compliance not effectively verified across organizational/software boundaries.
Transition from development/testing to operations left critical knowledge gaps.
Anomalous data existed but did not trigger a sufficiently forceful investigation before loss.
decisions_that_mattered: Use of ground-software AMD files once file-format problems were fixed without catching the unit mismatch.
Not executing TCM-5 before MOI despite late discussion.
Not having a process that surfaced and resolved the unit discrepancy while the mission was still recoverable.
recommendations_extracted: Verify consistent use of units throughout spacecraft design and operations.
Audit software-interface-specification compliance for data transferred between navigation and spacecraft-operations teams.
Validate small-forces models and compare navigation methods to uncover mismodeled forces.
Prepare and train for contingency trajectory-correction maneuvers.
counterfactuals_source_grounded: A source-level units audit could have exposed the Newton-second / pound-force-second mismatch.
A prepared TCM-5 decision and execution path might have provided a late recovery option; this remains framed as a board recommendation, not a proven rescue.
